questions.question: How long does it typically take to recover from a Google core update?
questions.answer_summary: Estimates vary by source: commonly cited as 1-3 months overall, 4-12 weeks for content/authority-driven issues, and up to 3-9 months across one or two full update cycles for harder cases.

questions.question: Why did my small business site lose rankings after the update?
questions.answer_summary: Cited causes include thin/repetitive template pages (e.g., near-identical suburb or city pages), weak trust signals, and a lack of visible expertise signals.

questions.question: What should I do first after being hit by a core update?
questions.answer_summary: Advice is calm review rather than panic edits — assess content quality, intent alignment, and trust signals before making sweeping changes.

questions.question: Do technical fixes speed up recovery?
questions.answer_summary: If the drop was technical in origin, improvement can appear within days; content/authority-related drops take much longer to resolve.

questions.question: Will my site only recover once the next core update rolls out?
questions.answer_summary: Yes in many cases — Google is described as re-evaluating previously impacted sites during the next core update cycle, so improvements often need to be in place before that next update.

questions.question: What concrete actions correlate with sites regaining rankings?
questions.answer_summary: Commonly cited actions: improving topical authority, cleaning up content architecture, adding structured data, and adding trust signals like a clear About page, contact details, and credentials/awards.

questions.question: Does removing thin/low-quality content help recovery?
questions.answer_summary: A cited case reported a site removing roughly 180 weak articles (about 20-30% of its weakest content) and recovering to about 85% of pre-update traffic levels within three weeks.

questions.question: How severe have recent core-update traffic drops been for smaller/niche sites?
questions.answer_summary: Some site owners reported drops of roughly 40-85%, concentrated among smaller niche sites.

questions.question: Are local businesses affected differently than other sites?
questions.answer_summary: Yes — cited local-specific causes include coasting on legacy citation volume/review counts without active profile management, and using generic rather than hyper-local content.

questions.question: Does Google Business Profile optimization play a role in local recovery?
questions.answer_summary: Yes, GBP optimization is presented as part of the local-SEO recovery response alongside on-site content and trust-signal work.

questions.question: How many sites are typically affected by a given core update?
questions.answer_summary: One estimate for the May 2026 core update put the share of sites with noticeable ranking changes at over 55%.

questions.question: Is a core update the same thing as a manual action/penalty?
questions.answer_summary: No — sources distinguish core updates (algorithmic, broad reassessments) from manual penalties, which changes the recovery approach since there's no 'reconsideration request' path for a core update.
